entries.title: Morning Briefing · 19 November 2026
headlines: Trump, Xi and Putin meet in Shenzhen today for the first-ever three-way US-China-Russia summit
Anthropic prices its IPO at $83, above range, and starts trading on Nasdaq today as ANT
Fed minutes point to more US rate rises; the Dow fell 1.1% and gold hit a 14-month low
Cyclone Akvan to cross the Andhra-Odisha coast on Friday; IMD issues red alerts
World Court rules today on the Rohingya genocide case against Myanmar from 09:00 GMT

stories.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin gather for a three-way summit in Shenzhen
stories.summary: On the APEC sidelines, the three leaders meet today after Trump and Putin were seated either side of Xi at Wednesday's welcome banquet. Expected topics include the Iran war, Ukraine, nuclear weapons, trade and AI. No outcomes had been reported at the time of writing.
stories.whyItMatters: A first meeting of this kind could set the tone on Ukraine and the Gulf conflict, both of which move oil prices and markets.

stories.headline: ICJ to give its judgment in the Rohingya genocide case at 09:00 GMT
stories.summary: The Gambia, backed by the OIC, accuses Myanmar of genocide over the 2017 military crackdown that drove at least 730,000 Rohingya from their homes. Myanmar denies it. The ruling, read in The Hague, cannot be appealed.
stories.whyItMatters: The court has never found a state responsible for genocide; a finding would also be read closely for the separate Gaza case.

stories.headline: Berlin hosts Ukraine talks the same day
stories.summary: German Chancellor Merz is due to host a Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin today, with US envoys and Ukrainian officials expected to coordinate on security guarantees. The exact line-up has not been confirmed.
stories.whyItMatters: Europe and Kyiv want a common position in place while Trump and Putin are meeting in China.

stories.headline: UAE tanker hit in Hormuz; US says Iranian attacks on Gulf bases intercepted
stories.summary: An ADNOC tanker was struck in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday night, with one crew member missing and 11 injured. Bahrain and Kuwait said they intercepted Iranian drones and missiles, and US Central Command reported no US casualties.
stories.whyItMatters: Each strike on shipping raises insurance costs per transit and keeps energy prices volatile.

stories.headline: UK-EU leaders' summit is tomorrow
stories.summary: Starmer meets EU leaders on Friday 20 November for the summit both sides confirmed in October, when he said the status quo was not good enough. The government wants the meeting to deepen the post-Brexit reset of trade and security ties.
stories.whyItMatters: Any deal on trade checks could affect food prices and business costs, and it lands days after inflation rose to 3.6%.

stories.headline: Home Secretary tells police to stay out of politics
stories.summary: Speaking at a policing conference on Wednesday, Shabana Mahmood said parts of the old police anti-racism commitment were wrong and announced a new impartiality standard, to be drafted by the College of Policing and consulted on next year. She rejected claims of two-tier policing but accepted there had been examples of unequal treatment.
stories.whyItMatters: It sets the direction for how forces handle protests and politically charged cases.

stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan to make landfall between Andhra Pradesh and Odisha on Friday
stories.summary: IMD expects the storm to cross the coast on 20 November with winds of up to about 110 km/h, and has issued red alerts for heavy rain. Rain has already started in Puri.
stories.whyItMatters: Coastal districts face flooding and evacuations; fishing and port activity on the east coast will be disrupted.

stories.headline: India-Japan 2+2 talks are under way in Tokyo today
stories.summary: Rajnath Singh and S Jaishankar meet Japan's foreign and defence ministers for the fourth 2+2 dialogue, covering defence technology, maritime security, exercises, critical minerals and semiconductors.
stories.whyItMatters: Japan is a key partner for defence manufacturing and supply chains as India hedges against China.

stories.headline: No new Immigration Rules overnight; earned settlement still awaits the December rules
stories.summary: No Statement of Changes has been published since HC 584 on 3 September. The earned settlement plan announced on 2 November, which moves the default route to ILR from 5 to 10 years with shorter paths for higher earners, is still a proposal and not in the rules. The Home Secretary has said the changes will begin to be laid from the December rules.
stories.whyItMatters: Skilled Workers, including many Indian nationals, should not assume any new ILR timeline applies until rule text and transitional dates are published.

stories.headline: Nicholls hundred rescues New Zealand on day one in Wellington
stories.summary: After Shubman Gill chose to bowl at the Basin Reserve, India reduced New Zealand to 74 for 5, with Jasprit Bumrah taking three wickets. Henry Nicholls made a century and Glenn Phillips reached 94 not out as the hosts closed on 243 for 5.
stories.whyItMatters: India let a strong start slip in the first Test of a series that carries World Test Championship points. Day two begins tonight UK time.

stories.headline: Pochettino starts work at Manchester United
stories.summary: Mauricio Pochettino has arrived at the club to begin his job as head coach, days after United confirmed his appointment following Michael Carrick's sacking.
stories.whyItMatters: He gets only days with the squad before his first league match in charge.

stories.headline: ISRO chief says the first uncrewed Gaganyaan flight is set for December
stories.summary: Chairman V Narayanan says G1 will launch from Sriharikota on the human-rated LVM3 in December, carrying the robot Vyommitra rather than astronauts. It will test the crew module, re-entry, parachutes and a splashdown in the Bay of Bengal.
stories.whyItMatters: G1 has slipped several times since 2024; a December flight would keep India's first crewed spaceflight in view for 2027.

stories.headline: Hawkish Fed minutes drag the Dow down 1.1%
stories.summary: Wednesday 18 Nov closes: Dow 50,198.17 (-1.11%), S&P 500 7,323.63 (-0.23%, a fifth straight fall), Nasdaq Composite 24,429.89 (+0.42%). Minutes showed almost all Fed officials saw more rate rises as likely; health insurers slumped on a proposed Medicare Advantage audit rule and Nvidia closed almost 3% lower.
stories.whyItMatters: Higher US rates hold up global borrowing costs; gold fell to a 14-month low on the news.

stories.headline: FTSE 100 closed 1.3% lower as miners slid
stories.summary: The FTSE 100 closed Wednesday 18 Nov at 10,551.17 (-1.30%). Antofagasta, Anglo American and Glencore fell 6 to 8% as copper and silver dropped on a stronger dollar and doubts about AI infrastructure spending.
stories.whyItMatters: London's heavy weighting in miners makes it sensitive to metal prices and the dollar.

stories.headline: Sensex and Nifty recover from early losses
stories.summary: Live at 10:52 IST on Thursday 19 Nov, still trading: Sensex 82,255.10 (+0.27%), Nifty 50 25,300.75 (+0.29%), after opening lower on the Fed minutes and weak IT stocks. Autos led the recovery, helped by PSU banks, easier oil and steady foreign buying.
stories.whyItMatters: Foreign investors bought about 5,867 crore rupees of shares on Wednesday, cushioning the market against global rate worries.

stories.headline: Anthropic priced at $83 a share ahead of today's debut
stories.summary: The AI company priced its offering above the 70 to 78 dollar range, and its registration was declared effective on Wednesday evening. Shares are expected to begin trading on Nasdaq today under the ticker ANT.
stories.whyItMatters: One of the largest listings on record will test investor appetite for AI stocks after a week of chip-sector selling.

entries.title: Evening Briefing · 18 November 2026
headlines: UK inflation rises to 3.6%, a one-year high, as diesel hits a record and a December rate rise stays likely
Xi greets Trump in Shenzhen as APEC opens; first Trump-Xi-Putin meeting planned for Thursday
Kuwait and Bahrain report drone attacks after the US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island
FTSE 100 drops another 1.3% to 10,551 as metals slump; Wall Street mixed, Nvidia lower despite beat
Cyclone Akvan weakens but turns towards Odisha, with landfall expected near Narsapur-Puri around noon Friday

stories.headline: Trump arrives at APEC in Shenzhen; trilateral with Xi and Putin set for Thursday
stories.summary: Xi Jinping greeted Donald Trump in person at Shenzhen airport as the APEC summit opened. A first-ever three-way meeting with Vladimir Putin is planned for Thursday. In Manila earlier, Trump announced a very big trade deal with the Philippines but gave no details.
stories.whyItMatters: The meeting could set the tone on tariffs, arms control and Ukraine for months. The Philippines deal is so far only Trump's claim.

stories.headline: Kuwait and Bahrain report drone attacks after the US strike on Qeshm
stories.summary: After the US strike on an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island, Kuwait says its air defences intercepted hostile drones and Bahrain blamed Iran for new aerial attacks. Neither has given damage or casualty figures.
stories.whyItMatters: The attacks now reach several Gulf states, so shipping and oil remain exposed. Most accounts so far come from one side only.

stories.headline: Drone strikes reportedly cut Russia's oil refining by almost half
stories.summary: Reuters, citing industry sources, reports that Ukrainian drone attacks have nearly halved Russia's oil refining in November. There are no official figures to confirm it.
stories.whyItMatters: If accurate, it is the heaviest pressure yet on Russian fuel supply and export income.

stories.headline: Inflation hits 3.6% in October as diesel sets a record
stories.summary: CPI rose to 3.6% from 3.5%, a one-year high, and CPIH rose to 3.7%, driven by motor fuels and tobacco. Diesel averaged 199.5p a litre, the highest since records began in 1996. Core inflation stayed at 2.8% and services at 3.7%, both slightly below forecasts.
stories.whyItMatters: Markets still put about a 74% chance on another Bank Rate rise in December, with Bank Rate at 4.00% after the 5 November rise.

stories.headline: Home Office sets out its legal basis for live facial recognition in immigration enforcement
stories.summary: On 17 November the Home Office published a policy paper on the legal mandate for Immigration Enforcement to use live facial recognition, with an equality impact assessment.
stories.whyItMatters: It shows the technology is being used beyond policing and is likely to draw scrutiny from privacy groups.

stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan downgraded, but its track now points at the Andhra-Odisha coast
stories.summary: IMD now expects a severe cyclonic storm with winds of 90 to 100 km/h, gusting to 110 km/h, making landfall between Narsapur and Puri around noon on Friday 20 November. That is further north than earlier forecasts. Odisha has sent out 74 rescue teams and listed more than 200,000 people for possible evacuation.
stories.whyItMatters: Weather models still disagree on the track and strength, but heavy rain is expected across Odisha.

stories.headline: Rajnath and Jaishankar in Tokyo ahead of Thursday's 2+2
stories.summary: The defence and external affairs ministers arrived in Tokyo for the fourth India-Japan 2+2 with Shinjiro Koizumi and Toshimitsu Motegi. At Raisina Tokyo, Jaishankar urged audiences to update their picture of India. No outcomes have been announced yet.
stories.whyItMatters: Coming straight after the Quad summit, any deals on defence equipment or maritime security would strengthen India-Japan ties.

stories.headline: No change to the Immigration Rules today
stories.summary: We found no new Statement of Changes and no visa, settlement or fee announcements on GOV.UK from 16 to 18 November. The latest rules change we know of is HC 584 of 3 September. The Immigration and Asylum Bill now goes to the Lords and is not yet law.
stories.whyItMatters: Skilled Worker and ILR applications still follow the current rules until new rules are laid.

stories.headline: Earned settlement: announced on 2 November, still not in the rules
stories.summary: The plan makes 10 years the default route to ILR, with 5 years for people earning at least 50,271 pounds in three of five years and 3 years for those earning 125,141 pounds or more. No Statement of Changes, start date or transitional arrangements have been published. A separate rule already in force requires B2-level English for settlement on specified routes from 26 March 2027.
stories.whyItMatters: For Indian Skilled Workers close to five years, the salary test and the transitional rules will decide when they can settle.

stories.headline: India's Test series in New Zealand starts tonight with WTC points at stake
stories.summary: The first Test at the Basin Reserve starts at 22:00 GMT (03:30 IST Thursday), with Shubman Gill captaining India and Tom Latham leading New Zealand, who top the WTC table. India are fourth and need six wins from their last seven Tests to reach the final without relying on other results.
stories.whyItMatters: India have a poor record in New Zealand, and the result could decide their WTC hopes.

stories.headline: Premier League returns this weekend with Arsenal five points clear
stories.summary: Arsenal lead the table on 27 points, five ahead of Brighton, and play away at Newcastle at 17:30 on Saturday.
stories.whyItMatters: St James' Park is one of the hardest away trips for the leaders this season.

stories.headline: NASA ends two veteran science missions: Terra and NICER
stories.summary: NASA says the Earth-observing satellite Terra will stop collecting science data on 1 December, after 27 years. The NICER X-ray telescope on the ISS has ended science operations after about six and a half years.
stories.whyItMatters: Terra's records underpin decades of climate and land-use research.

stories.headline: Roman Space Telescope's first images will be shown on 7 December
stories.summary: NASA will stream the first images from the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope live from the AGU meeting on Monday 7 December.
stories.whyItMatters: The first images will show whether the telescope built to survey dark energy and exoplanets is working as designed.

stories.headline: FTSE 100 falls 1.3% as miners slump
stories.summary: The FTSE 100 closed 138.70 points lower at 10,551.17 (16:35 GMT close), after Tuesday's 1.76% fall. Falling copper, gold and silver and a 19-month high in the dollar sent Antofagasta down 7.9%, Anglo American down 7.2% and Glencore down 6.1%. Convatec rose 9.4% and Hays jumped 39% in the FTSE 250.
stories.whyItMatters: London has lost about 3% in two sessions as doubts about copper demand from AI and higher interest-rate expectations hit commodity stocks.

stories.headline: Sensex and Nifty end a two-day rally
stories.summary: At the 15:30 IST close the Sensex was down about 500 points (0.61%) at 82,031.81 and the Nifty 50 was near 25,228 (down 0.63%), on profit-taking. Consumer durables were the weakest sector and metal stocks fell with global prices.
stories.whyItMatters: The fall in global metal prices and a stronger dollar are both putting pressure on Indian markets.

stories.headline: Wall Street mixed; Nvidia lower despite strong results
stories.summary: Still trading at 13:19 ET: the Dow was down 0.94% at 50,282, the S&P 500 down 0.15% at 7,329 and the Nasdaq Composite up 0.37% at 24,419. Nvidia lost about 2.4% despite doubling its revenue, Fed governor Waller said a half-point December hike is probably needed, and UnitedHealth fell about 6%.
stories.whyItMatters: Expectations of higher US rates are outweighing strong AI earnings. The Fed's October minutes are due at 19:00 GMT.

stories.headline: Anthropic IPO expected to price tonight
stories.summary: Anthropic is expected to set its share price tonight, against a range of 70 to 78 dollars, with Nasdaq trading due to start on Thursday under the ticker ANT, subject to regulatory clearance. CNBC reports, citing sources, that it may enlarge the offering because of strong demand.
stories.whyItMatters: At the top of the range it would be one of the largest listings ever and a test of investor appetite for AI.

entries.title: Morning Briefing · 18 November 2026
headlines: Nvidia beats and guides to about 130 billion dollars; shares up nearly 5 percent after hours
US hits an IRGC missile site on Iran's Qeshm Island after drones target a base in Bahrain
Commons passes the Immigration and Asylum Bill 290 to 94; it now goes to the Lords
Quad leaders agree five initiatives in Manila, with India to host a business forum in 2027
UK October inflation is out at 07:00, forecast at 3.6 percent with a December rate rise priced in

stories.headline: US strikes an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island
stories.summary: US aircraft struck an IRGC missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island on Tuesday evening, a US military official said, describing it as self-defence. It followed an IRGC drone attack on Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain that CENTCOM says was intercepted with no US damage. Iranian officials say no homes or infrastructure were hit and report no casualties.
stories.whyItMatters: A direct US strike on Iranian soil in the Strait of Hormuz raises the risk of a wider exchange while mediated talks are stalled. There is no on-record Pentagon statement yet.

stories.headline: Hormuz: more tanker damage, talks stuck
stories.summary: Iran's navy says five tankers were damaged by mines in 24 hours, including a supertanker and an LPG carrier; the UK's maritime agency UKMTO has independently reported two attacks on tankers near Khasab, Oman. Washington has rejected Iran's seven conditions for reopening the strait, and Qatar, Pakistan and Turkey are still mediating.
stories.whyItMatters: The mine figures come only from Iran, but shipping risk is keeping Brent near 92 dollars, which feeds into UK and Indian inflation.

stories.headline: Ukraine hits two Russian refineries; Europe adds money
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones reportedly struck the Ilsky and Afipsky refineries in Russia's Krasnodar region overnight. Norway and Sweden pledged more than 370 million dollars for weapons, and the EU is reported to be preparing a further 45 billion euros for Ukraine. Germany and the UK pushed back after a senior US official criticised Ukraine's long-range strikes.
stories.whyItMatters: This comes ahead of Thursday's Berlin talks on the next phase of negotiations with Russia, and shows Europe and Washington pulling in different directions.

stories.headline: APEC opens in Shenzhen with a Trump-Xi meeting due
stories.summary: The two-day APEC summit begins today in Shenzhen. Trump is due to meet Xi on Thursday and says he is open to separate talks with Putin in China. The White House says he wants to raise nuclear arms reduction.
stories.whyItMatters: New US curbs on AI chip exports, announced on Monday, will shadow the talks. Beijing has already objected.

stories.headline: October inflation due at 07:00
stories.summary: The ONS publishes October CPI at 07:00. The consensus forecast is 3.6 percent, up from 3.5 percent in September, driven by fuel, energy and tobacco. Bank Rate is 4.00 percent after a rise on 5 November.
stories.whyItMatters: A figure above forecast would make a second rate rise in December almost certain, which would push up mortgage and loan costs.

stories.headline: Unemployment falls to 4.6 percent, vacancies at a five-year low
stories.summary: Tuesday's figures showed unemployment at 4.6 percent in the three months to September, better than the 4.7 percent expected, with employment up 155,000. Wage growth eased to 3.6 percent and vacancies fell to their lowest level since 2021.
stories.whyItMatters: Traders now see about a 90 percent chance of a December rate rise, which leaves this morning's inflation figure as the deciding piece of data.

stories.headline: Quad summit: five outcomes, India to host a business forum
stories.summary: Modi, Trump, Albanese and Takaichi met in Manila on Tuesday for the 7th Quad leaders' summit, the first in two years. They announced joint maritime surveillance with P-8 and P-3C aircraft in 2027, cable and cyber cooperation, and counter-terrorism work that condemns cross-border terrorism. Mumbai will host the first Quad Business Leaders' Forum in early 2027.
stories.whyItMatters: The statement's warning about economic coercion through export restrictions is aimed at supply-chain pressure. No separate Modi-Trump trade deal was announced.

stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan heads for Andhra, landfall Friday
stories.summary: The IMD expects Akvan to become a very severe cyclonic storm by Thursday night and to cross the coast between Nellore and Tuni by noon on 20 November, with winds of 120 to 130 km/h gusting to 145 km/h. Odisha has begun early evacuations in southern districts, and fishermen across Andhra and Tamil Nadu have been told to stay ashore.
stories.whyItMatters: This would be Andhra Pradesh's third cyclone in three weeks, on ground that is already saturated.

stories.headline: Rajnath and Jaishankar in Tokyo for India-Japan 2+2
stories.summary: The defence and external affairs ministers are in Japan on 18 and 19 November for the fourth foreign and defence ministers' dialogue, which meets on Thursday. Defence industry ties, maritime security and the Indo-Pacific are on the agenda.
stories.whyItMatters: It follows straight on from the Quad summit and could bring defence-equipment or technology agreements.

stories.headline: Immigration and Asylum Bill clears the Commons
stories.summary: MPs passed the bill at Third Reading on Tuesday by 290 votes to 94, with 14 Labour MPs voting against. It would remove the five-working-day notice before removals, cut refugees' first grant of leave from five years to 30 months and create an independent immigration appeals body. An amendment to extend five-year settlement to more skilled workers was defeated 368 to 44.
stories.whyItMatters: It is not law yet: the Lords must pass it and it then needs Royal Assent, and no commencement dates have been set. For Skilled Worker visa holders, the failed amendment means the earned-settlement plan's longer default route stands.

stories.headline: No new Immigration Rules; earned settlement start date still not set
stories.summary: We found no new Statement of Changes since HC 584 of 3 September. Under the earned-settlement plan announced on 2 November, the default route to ILR becomes 10 years, cut to 5 years for people earning over 50,271 pounds and for some public-service roles, and 3 years for the highest earners. Care workers earning 25,000 pounds or more keep 5 years.
stories.whyItMatters: These are announced policy, not rules in force. Nothing changes for applicants until a Statement of Changes is laid. People who already have ILR keep it.

stories.headline: India's first Test in New Zealand starts tonight
stories.summary: The first of two Tests starts at the Basin Reserve in Wellington at 22:00 GMT tonight, which is 03:30 IST on Thursday. The second Test is at Hagley Oval in Christchurch from 26 November. New Zealand are without Mitchell Santner.
stories.whyItMatters: India arrive having won the ODI series 3-1, and both Tests count towards the World Test Championship.

stories.headline: MS Dhoni ends IPL playing career, becomes CSK mentor
stories.summary: MS Dhoni has retired as an IPL player and will mentor Chennai Super Kings from the 2027 season.
stories.whyItMatters: It ends the playing career of the league's best-known captain. He stays with CSK in a guiding role.

stories.headline: Nations League: Ireland finish second, Wales lose to Portugal
stories.summary: The Republic of Ireland beat 10-man Kosovo 3-0, with two penalties from Troy Parrott, to finish second in their group. That earns a March play-off for promotion to League A and a place in pot two for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw. Wales lost 2-3 to 10-man Portugal and finished bottom of Group A4. Northern Ireland drew 1-1 in Hungary, and Scotland lost 4-0 in Switzerland on Monday.
stories.whyItMatters: The league phase is over. The knockout and play-off draw is on Friday at 11:00 GMT.

stories.headline: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth today
stories.summary: At about 10:16 GMT today NASA's Voyager 1 will be one light-day away, about 25.9 billion km, the first human-made object to get that far. A signal will take 24 hours to reach it. The spacecraft launched in 1977, and most of its instruments are now switched off.
stories.whyItMatters: The milestone shows how long the probe has outlasted its design life. Voyager 2 is not expected to reach the same distance until 2035.

stories.headline: Nvidia beats forecasts and guides higher
stories.summary: For the quarter to 25 October, Nvidia reported revenue of 115.8 billion dollars, up 103 percent on a year earlier, and earnings per share of 2.68 dollars against about 2.47 dollars expected. It guided to about 130 billion dollars for the current quarter, which has an extra week and assumes no China data-centre sales. The shares rose about 4.8 percent after hours.
stories.whyItMatters: The AI trade hinges on Nvidia. A beat steadies chip stocks after a sharp November sell-off, but the inquiry into former CEO Jensen Huang, where nothing has been found against him, and the export curbs remain.

stories.headline: Wall Street falls before Nvidia; futures recover a little
stories.summary: On Tuesday the Dow fell 1.6 percent, about 848 points. The S&P 500 fell 1.0 percent to its lowest close since late July, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.7 percent after being down as much as 2.1 percent during the day. Chipmakers were sold ahead of Nvidia's results, and a reported outage on an NSA network added to the nerves. Overnight, S&P futures were up about 0.2 percent and Nasdaq-100 futures about 0.5 percent.
stories.whyItMatters: The Nasdaq-100 is on course for its worst November since 2008, and the VIX volatility index is above 25.

stories.headline: FTSE 100 has its worst day in eight months
stories.summary: The FTSE 100 closed down 1.76 percent at 10,689.87 on Tuesday, and the FTSE 250 fell 1.2 percent. Banks led the losses (Barclays down 2.6 percent, HSBC down 2 percent), followed by miners on weaker copper. Burberry fell 3.5 percent, and Imperial Brands lost 2 percent after announcing up to 4,600 job cuts by 2030.
stories.whyItMatters: London is likely to open firmer if Nvidia's beat holds, but the inflation figure at 07:00 could move gilts and the banks.

stories.headline: Sensex and Nifty slip as investors take profits
stories.summary: On Tuesday the Sensex rose 427 points (0.52 percent) to 82,532.19 and the Nifty rose 0.38 percent to 25,387.40. At 12:00 IST on Wednesday, still trading, the Sensex was at 82,122.47 (down 0.50 percent) and the Nifty at 25,248.30 (down 0.55 percent). Titan, TCS and metal stocks led the falls, as investors took profits after a rally of about 13 percent in 12 sessions.
stories.whyItMatters: Foreign investors have bought a record of about 10 billion dollars of Indian shares in November. Profit-taking at these levels is normal and does not reverse that trend.

stories.headline: Asia mixed despite the Nvidia beat
stories.summary: At about 02:30 GMT the Nikkei was down 0.3 percent at 58,697, the Kospi down 0.2 percent and the Hang Seng down 0.5 percent. Taiwan's index was down about 2 percent an hour later. Chip-equipment makers such as Tokyo Electron fell, while SK Hynix rose.
stories.whyItMatters: New US licence rules for AI-chip exports to five countries, and Nvidia's outlook excluding China, are limiting the lift for Asian chipmakers.

entries.title: Evening Briefing · 17 November 2026
headlines: Stocks slide ahead of Nvidia results
Ukraine strike damages the Kerch Bridge
UK sanctions eight Israeli settlement builders
Cyclone Akvan strengthens in the Bay of Bengal
Iran says it targeted a US radar in Bahrain

stories.headline: Kerch Bridge damaged in Ukrainian operation
stories.summary: Zelenskyy praised an operation that damaged the bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea. Images reportedly show a span in the water, which has not been independently verified, and the Kremlin says it will rebuild.
stories.whyItMatters: The bridge is a key supply route for Russian forces in southern Ukraine, and the strike comes days before new talks.

stories.headline: Ukraine security talks planned in Berlin on Thursday
stories.summary: US envoys Witkoff and Kushner are due to meet Ukrainian and European officials on 19 November on security guarantees and reconstruction. Moscow says it has not agreed to European participation in the next round.
stories.whyItMatters: It is the next concrete step on the peace track, and Russia's objection shows friction over who takes part.

stories.headline: Iran claims drone attack on a US radar in Bahrain
stories.summary: The IRGC said it targeted a radar at the Sheikh Isa air base. Bahrain says the drones were intercepted with no casualties or damage.
stories.whyItMatters: A claimed strike on a US facility raises the risk of escalation in the Gulf and keeps oil prices on edge.

stories.headline: Mongolia's president says he will resign
stories.summary: President Khurelsukh announced he will step down after a former Ulaanbaatar mayor accused him of receiving $25m linked to a railway project. He denies wrongdoing and the claim is unproven.
stories.whyItMatters: It opens a leadership transition in a country balanced between Russia and China.

stories.headline: Canada and China agree further tariff cuts
stories.summary: Xi and Carney agreed that China will ease tariffs on about $280m of Canadian exports, while Canada extends exemptions on some Chinese steel and aluminium for two years.
stories.whyItMatters: It continues the thaw in Canada-China trade amid wider tariff tension with the US.

stories.headline: Israel: allegations of election-day meddling
stories.summary: Reports allege Netanyahu's camp passed on information that led to the arrest of Arab party workers on election day. Prime Minister-elect Gadi Eisenkot has called for an investigation, and the claims are not officially confirmed.
stories.whyItMatters: The allegations could overshadow the transfer of power after Israel's election.

stories.headline: UK sanctions Israeli settlement builders and aid-blocking activists
stories.summary: The government is sanctioning eight Israeli construction firms building in West Bank settlements, along with an activist group that obstructs aid into Gaza. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband announced the measures.
stories.whyItMatters: It is one of the UK's toughest steps yet on settlements and puts the Burnham government at odds with Israel's government.

stories.headline: Burnham says Brexit has cost the UK more than it gained
stories.summary: In his Lord Mayor's Banquet speech, Andy Burnham argued for closer EU ties and said he will talk with EU leaders after Friday's UK-EU reset summit, while hinting at a slower timeline.
stories.whyItMatters: It is the clearest sign yet of how far the new prime minister wants to move on EU relations.

stories.headline: Russia warns the UK over its 2027 G20 summit
stories.summary: After London said Putin will not attend the summit it hosts during its 2027 G20 presidency, Russia's G20 envoy warned of serious consequences if he is kept out.
stories.whyItMatters: The row could complicate the UK's G20 year before it begins.

stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan strengthens, Andhra landfall expected on 20 November
stories.summary: IMD placed the storm about 610 km east of Chennai on Tuesday morning and expects it to become a very severe cyclonic storm by the evening of 19 November, crossing the Andhra Pradesh-Yanam coast around noon on 20 November. Odisha has begun evacuating vulnerable areas and five Andhra districts are on orange alert.
stories.whyItMatters: Coastal Andhra and Odisha face heavy rain, strong winds and disruption to travel and farming later this week.

stories.headline: Delhi air stays very poor as GRAP Stage III continues
stories.summary: Delhi's AQI read 288 overnight, with some stations above 300, and the early-warning system forecasts very poor air for about six more days. Stage III restrictions remain in force across the NCR.
stories.whyItMatters: Construction curbs and health advisories are likely to stay in place into next week.

stories.headline: Modi addresses the ASEAN-India Summit in Manila
stories.summary: At the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit, Modi linked India's growth to ASEAN's prosperity, tying ASEAN Vision 2045 to India's 2047 goals and pointing to Act East outcomes.
stories.whyItMatters: It frames India's push for deeper trade and security ties in Southeast Asia.

stories.headline: No new Immigration Rules changes this week
stories.summary: GOV.UK shows no new Statement of Changes, fee change, or Skilled Worker or Graduate rule change between 10 and 17 November. The latest Statement of Changes is still HC 584, published on 3 September 2026.
stories.whyItMatters: There is nothing new for people on work visas to act on today; the sponsor register had a routine update on 12 November.

stories.headline: Earned settlement: start date still not set
stories.summary: The Home Secretary's 2 November announcement, updated on 13 November, sets settlement at 3 years for top earners, 5 years above £50,271 and for some public-service workers, a 10-year default, and 20 years or more for rule breakers. GOV.UK gives no rules reference or start date yet.
stories.whyItMatters: Many Skilled Worker visa holders on the 5-year ILR path could be affected, so watch for a Statement of Changes with transition rules.

stories.headline: Santner ruled out of the New Zealand-India Tests
stories.summary: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner has a hand fracture and misses the two-Test series against India, with Dean Foxcroft called up. The first Test starts at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on 19 November.
stories.whyItMatters: It weakens New Zealand's spin attack after India's white-ball leg finished on 15 November.

stories.headline: Jay Shah re-appointed ICC chair until 2030
stories.summary: Shah was returned unopposed at the ICC Board meetings in Bali.
stories.whyItMatters: It keeps Indian leadership at the top of world cricket through the 2030 cycle.

stories.headline: Nations League: home nations in action tonight
stories.summary: Wales v Portugal, Republic of Ireland v Kosovo, Hungary v Northern Ireland and Ukraine v Georgia all kick off at 19:45 GMT. England finished their window in Spain on Sunday, and England's third ODI against Australia is in Hobart on 18 November.
stories.whyItMatters: Tonight's results settle group placings before club football returns this weekend.

stories.headline: Sentinel-6B cleared as the sea-level reference satellite
stories.summary: NASA says Sentinel-6B has been calibrated and passed its initial checks, ready to take over the long-running ocean height record.
stories.whyItMatters: Its data underpins the global sea-level rise measurements used in climate planning.

stories.headline: ISRO's Gaganyaan-1 still targeted for this quarter
stories.summary: The uncrewed Gaganyaan-1 flight carrying the Vyommitra robot is still planned for the fourth quarter of 2026, but no launch date has been announced.
stories.whyItMatters: It is the key test before India's first crewed spaceflight.

stories.headline: FTSE 100 falls 1.8% ahead of Nvidia
stories.summary: London closed at 10,689.87, down 191.68 points (−1.8%), and the FTSE 250 fell 1.2%. Tech losses, hotter-than-expected US import and export prices and a pullback in defence stocks such as BAE (−2.5%) weighed.

stories.headline: Sensex and Nifty extend gains as Bank Nifty hits a record
stories.summary: The Sensex closed at 82,532.19 (+0.52%) and the Nifty 50 at 25,387.40 (+0.38%), with Bank Nifty up 1.13% to a record 62,273. Brent easing to around $92, strong foreign buying and money moving out of global tech helped, while IT stocks fell about 0.9%.

stories.headline: Wall Street lower in the Nvidia countdown
stories.summary: At 13:03 ET the S&P 500 was at 7,331.04 (−1.15%), the Dow at 50,835.79 (−1.50%) and the Nasdaq Composite at 24,233.91 (−1.13%). October retail sales rose 0.2%, homebuilder sentiment hit its lowest since 2012, and Disney and Home Depot beat forecasts.
stories.whyItMatters: Nvidia reports after the bell, its first quarter without Jensen Huang as CEO, setting the tone for Asia and Europe on Wednesday.

entries.title: Morning Briefing · 17 November 2026
headlines: Trump starts Asia trip: Quad in Manila, then Xi and Putin in China
Third US carrier reaches the Middle East as Iran talks stall
Wall Street drops about 2% on AI and chip fears before Nvidia's results
Ukraine hits the Kerch Bridge in an overnight drone attack
England win 3-2 in Spain; India take ODI series in New Zealand 3-1

stories.headline: Trump heads to Manila for ASEAN and the Quad, then APEC in China
stories.summary: Trump left for the Philippines on Tuesday for ASEAN and the first Quad leaders' meeting in about two years, alongside Japan, Australia and India. He then travels to APEC in Shenzhen, where the Kremlin expects a three-way meeting with Xi and Putin on Thursday 19 November.
stories.whyItMatters: The Quad agenda covers maritime security, export controls, critical minerals and AI, all of direct interest to India. A Trump, Xi and Putin meeting would be a first.

stories.headline: Third US aircraft carrier arrives near Iran as talks stall
stories.summary: The USS Theodore Roosevelt has joined two other US carriers in the Middle East while talks on ending hostilities with Iran and reopening the Strait of Hormuz remain stuck. JD Vance said Trump will not let it become a long war, and an Iranian deputy foreign minister warned Tehran would not wait to be struck first.
stories.whyItMatters: The build-up raises the risk of renewed fighting. Disruption at Hormuz has kept Brent crude above $90, which feeds UK and Indian inflation.

stories.headline: Ukrainian drones hit the Kerch Bridge to Crimea
stories.summary: Ukraine struck the bridge between Russia and occupied Crimea overnight and traffic was briefly restricted. The Kremlin said it was assessing minor damage, while Russian air raids killed at least seven people in Kyiv.
stories.whyItMatters: The bridge is a key Russian supply route, and the strike comes as Kyiv says European officials have joined settlement negotiating teams for the first time. Accounts of the damage differ.

stories.headline: Japan scrambles jets as Russian aircraft enter its airspace
stories.summary: Two suspected Russian military aircraft entered Japanese airspace near Okinoshima early on Tuesday and Tokyo lodged a protest. South Korea also scrambled fighters when Russian planes entered its air defence zone, though not its territory.
stories.whyItMatters: It raises tension in North-East Asia days before Putin visits China and during Trump's trip to the region.

stories.headline: Houthis reported to control the Bab al-Mandab area
stories.summary: The BBC reports that Iran-backed Houthis have gained ground on the Red Sea coast after Saudi-backed government forces pulled back to defend Aden. Full Houthi control of the strait has not been independently confirmed.
stories.whyItMatters: About 12% of world trade passes through the strait, so together with Hormuz restrictions both Gulf shipping routes would be squeezed.

stories.headline: Five EU states explore a Rwanda return hub for rejected asylum seekers
stories.summary: Austria, Denmark, Germany, Greece and the Netherlands say they are negotiating a hub in Rwanda, aiming for first transfers in 2027 with room for about 100 people at first. Rights groups condemned the plan.
stories.whyItMatters: It revives an offshore model the UK abandoned and could shape European asylum policy, though nothing has been agreed.

stories.headline: UK jobs data today and inflation tomorrow, with rate rises in play
stories.summary: Official labour market figures are due on Tuesday morning and October CPI follows on Wednesday, with forecasts around 3.7% against 3.5% in September. Bank of England chief economist Huw Pill has signalled more rate rises may be needed.
stories.whyItMatters: A hot inflation reading would strengthen bets on a December hike, pushing mortgage and borrowing costs higher.

stories.headline: Peers say the UK is seriously underprepared for emergencies
stories.summary: A House of Lords committee says the UK is not ready for major emergencies and threats, and calls for a cabinet-level resilience minister within six months, changes to stockpiling and new stress-testing duties. The Cabinet Office said it would consider the report.
stories.whyItMatters: It adds pressure on the Burnham government over civil preparedness amid Middle East conflict and energy shocks.

stories.headline: Burnham expected to make the case for closer EU trade ties
stories.summary: A business news round-up says the Prime Minister will use his Lord Mayor's Banquet speech to argue for closer trading links with the EU, ahead of a UK-EU summit on Friday 20 November. The report comes from a single secondary source.
stories.whyItMatters: A shift on EU trade would be one of the new government's biggest policy signals.

stories.headline: Modi expected to meet Trump at the Quad in Manila
stories.summary: Modi travels to Manila for ASEAN meetings and the Quad summit, where he is expected to hold talks with Trump shortly before the US president meets Xi and Putin. Trade and maritime security are likely to top the agenda.
stories.whyItMatters: It is a chance to make progress with Washington on trade and tariffs, and to gauge India's position ahead of the US, China and Russia meeting.

stories.headline: Opposition asks Supreme Court to let it question the Election Commission over SIR
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders want the Supreme Court's permission to serve 48 formal written questions on the Election Commission about the Special Intensive Revision of voter rolls, with answers from named officials.
stories.whyItMatters: The voter-roll revision is a central political dispute, and the court's answer will decide how closely the Commission's process can be examined.

stories.headline: India raises windfall tax on diesel and jet fuel exports
stories.summary: The government has increased the windfall gains tax on exports of diesel and aviation turbine fuel, while the export duty on petrol remains zero.
stories.whyItMatters: With global fuel prices high, the tax keeps more supply at home and raises revenue, but it weighs on export-heavy refiners.

stories.headline: India votes against UN call for a global death-penalty moratorium
stories.summary: India voted against a UN General Assembly resolution urging a worldwide pause on executions, consistent with its past votes.
stories.whyItMatters: India continues to treat capital punishment as a matter for its own laws despite international pressure.

stories.headline: No new Immigration Rules changes since last week
stories.summary: No new Immigration Rules changes have been published since last week. The latest Statement of Changes is still HC 584 (3 September 2026), and earned settlement rules are due in a December Statement of Changes.

stories.headline: Earned settlement: announced, not yet in force
stories.summary: The Home Secretary set out the final design on 2 November: a 10-year default route to ILR, cut to 5 years for people earning at least £50,271 in three of the last five years or in eligible public-service jobs, and to 3 years at £125,141 or more. Graduate and Student time would not count.
stories.whyItMatters: For Skilled Workers, earnings history will matter more than current salary, and B2 English is expected from March 2027. Wait for the December rules and guidance before acting.

stories.headline: Immigration and Asylum Bill listed for final Commons stages today
stories.summary: The Commons schedule lists the bill's report stage and third reading for Tuesday 17 November, after which it moves to the Lords.
stories.whyItMatters: Amendments today could change asylum and enforcement law, though settlement thresholds sit in the Immigration Rules, not this bill.

stories.headline: India beat New Zealand by 22 runs to take the ODI series 3-1
stories.summary: India defended their total in the fifth ODI at Mount Maunganui on 15 November, with Arshdeep Singh and Axar Patel leading the bowling.
stories.whyItMatters: The win builds momentum before the two-Test series, which starts at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Thursday 19 November.

stories.headline: England win 3-2 away to Spain in the Nations League
stories.summary: England beat the world champions in Madrid on Sunday, following a 2-1 home win over Croatia on Thursday. It reverses September's 3-2 defeat to Spain at Wembley.
stories.whyItMatters: Two wins in four days leave England well placed in Nations League Group A3.

stories.headline: Crystal Palace appoint Thomas Frank as manager
stories.summary: The former Brentford and Tottenham manager has signed until June 2029, replacing Pierre Sage, who was sacked on 12 November with Palace bottom of the Premier League.
stories.whyItMatters: Palace need a quick turnaround to avoid relegation when the league resumes after the international break.

stories.headline: UEFA backs Philippe Diallo to challenge Infantino for FIFA president
stories.summary: European football's governing body unanimously backed the French federation president, who has accepted. The FIFA election is on 18 March 2027 in Rabat.
stories.whyItMatters: It is the first serious challenge to Infantino in years and puts UEFA at odds with FIFA's leadership.

stories.headline: ULA Vulcan failure destroys 40 Amazon Leo satellites
stories.summary: A Vulcan Centaur failed about 10 minutes after lift-off from Cape Canaveral on 15 November, and all 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites on board were lost.
stories.whyItMatters: It sets back Amazon's challenge to Starlink and ULA's launch schedule, including US government missions.

stories.headline: Starship Flight 15: conflicting reports on the tower catches
stories.summary: SpaceX flew Starship Flight 15 on 14 November. Space.com reports the launch tower caught the upper stage for the first time, but another report says the booster catch was called off, and details are not yet confirmed.
stories.whyItMatters: Catching both stages is key to fast, cheap reuse, which NASA's lunar lander plans depend on.

stories.headline: ISRO: no launch this week, Gaganyaan G1 still due by year end
stories.summary: ISRO has no launch scheduled this week, and the first uncrewed Gaganyaan test flight (G1) is still listed for the last quarter of 2026. The Leonid meteor shower peaks on the nights of 17 and 18 November.
stories.whyItMatters: G1 is the last major step before India's first crewed spaceflight.

stories.headline: Wall Street drops on AI and chip fears before Nvidia
stories.summary: On Monday the S&P 500 closed at 7,416.59 (−1.92%), the Dow at 51,608.17 (−1.41%) and the Nasdaq Composite at 24,509.76 (−2.49%). Chipmakers led the fall, with Nvidia −1.9%, AMD −3.8% and Intel −5.9%, on worries about AI valuations and tighter US curbs on Chinese access to Nvidia computing.
stories.whyItMatters: Nvidia reports after the US close on Tuesday under interim leadership following Jensen Huang's resignation. Asian markets were lower on Tuesday morning.

stories.headline: FTSE 100 gives up early gains as miners slide
stories.summary: The FTSE 100 closed Monday at 10,881.55 (−0.19%) after reaching 10,939 at midday. Weak Chinese data hit miners such as Anglo American (−4.3%) and Antofagasta (−3.1%), while Coca-Cola HBC rose 2.6% on plans for a Johannesburg listing.

stories.headline: Sensex and Nifty open higher on foreign buying and cheaper oil
stories.summary: At 09:27 IST on Tuesday the Sensex was at 82,221.25 (+0.14%) and the Nifty 50 at 25,327.15 (+0.14%), still trading. Foreign investors bought about ₹84,290 crore of Indian shares in the first half of November as money rotated out of Asian AI stocks.
stories.whyItMatters: Easing crude helps the rupee and the inflation outlook. Autos and PSU banks led early while IT lagged.
